articles.headline: Erik Spoelstra wants the Heat to embrace the media pressure after their slow start
keyFacts: The Miami Heat started the 2026-27 NBA season with a 4-6 record over their first ten games.
Coach Erik Spoelstra wants his players to embrace media pressure and use it to fuel their focus.
The Heat plan to continue working through their early defensive struggles as the regular season progresses.
body: The Miami Heat have played their first 10 games of the 2026-27 NBA season, and unfortunately, they are not off to a good start. They went 4-6 in this early-season stretch, but thankfully, they have 72 more games left to play in the regular season.

It has been a tough few weeks for the Heat to start the year, but there are some promising signs. In their 114-108 win against the Sacramento Kings on Sunday, the Heat showcased how they work as a proper squad. Giannis Antetokounmpo was the superstar, while Klay Thompson and Bam Adebayo served as his main running mates.
Erik Spoelstra urges the Heat's players to embrace the pressure the media has put on them

There was considerable hype surrounding the Heat when they traded for Antetokounmpo. Pairing him with Adebayo showed that they were serious about improving the defense and having a true superstar lead the charge on offense.

Only the latter has been present for the Heat so far this season because they are weirdly not in sync on defense just yet. Miami definitely has the potential to flip the switch and go on a big run. However, this has led to a big pile-on from the media over the past few weeks.

Coach Erik Spoelstra dislikes how the Heat have started this season, but he knows that the team is much better than what their 4-6 record suggests. That is why he wants his players to take in what the media is saying about them, and use it to fuel themselves.

"I tell the team to embrace the tension...we have ambitions, guys who wanna figure it out. What it does is that when you feel uncomfortable, it forces a laser collective focus. I love that. I love that feeling in the locker room," Spoelstra said after the Heat's win against Sacramento.

Moving forward, the Heat should be a tougher team to play against. They are finding their stride slowly but surely. It will be a process, but with how motivated they look, they will be a dangerous team in the long run.

articles.headline: Words of Prey, Seahawks-Cardinals: Defense, offense both Locked in
keyFacts: The Seattle Seahawks defeated the Arizona Cardinals 17-3 in a game dominated by the Seattle defense and a mistake-free offense.
Running back Zach Charbonnet contributed significantly on the ground, helping the Seahawks secure the win and manage the game clock in the fourth quarter.
Seattle's defense limited Arizona's scoring opportunities, stopping a late fourth-quarter threat inside the five-yard line to seal the victory.
body: Looks like the rule against owning multiple NFL franchises doesn’t apply to Vinod Khosla.

Not after the Seattle Seahawks re-demolished their rivals from the desert 17-3 in a game that could’ve been closer, I suppose, but also could’ve easily been a much wider blowout. Truthfully, only a couple main outcomes were on the table today in Seahawks-Cardinals II: Defensive Boogaloo: A) Narrow Arizona victory aided by touchdown drives and various balderdash (including but not limited to officiating shenanigans), or B) Return-to-form Seattle win reminiscent of Week 8 against the Chiefs and *waves at entire Mike Macdonald era*.

We very nearly got A), but instead, it was indeed B), a Macdonald lab-grown triumph via timely contributions from your remaining defensive stars, excellent containment of explosives, and mistake-free offense. Watching the defense, was, as ever, a series of little climaxes leading to the sweet release of victory formation.

The Seahawks had one favorable officiating decision (the Barner TD reception) outweighed by several unfavorable ones, which kept leading to score changes, and still prevailed by two touchdowns, undermanned, without Jaxon Smith-Njigba being the main reason, either. I’ll tell you: I came into Week 9 weirdly excited. We were going to see the Hawks win extremely shorthanded and confirm that they still have a role to play in the NFC, or they’d lose and spend at least one week at the bottom of the division, underwater at 4-5 and 1-2.

They won’t be spending that week in the cellar and we won’t spend the week thinking about draft targets. In part because the red zone woes flipped; in part because Drew Lock was up to managing the game flawlessly; and as usual, in largest part because it’s so dang hard to score against them. You need a lot of things to go right in the proper sequence, and the Cardinals didn’t have the weapons beyond Trey McBride to pull off the upset.

They did receive more than their fair share of breaks, such as Reggie Virgil’s third-down bobble being ruled a catch on the opening possession or Josh Jobe’s interception being nullified because Trey McBride can’t run in a straight line without falling down:

It feels fan-conceited to say, but the Seahawks defense is so complete (and so deep! Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu didn’t even suit up!) that they could pitch a shutout every time they take the field. Remember the Super Bowl? I’d guess yeah. The Patriots got some garbage points in the fourth quarter and put up a big goose egg until then.
There’s nobody this Seahawks defense can’t dominate. Give them another shot at the Bears in January, NFL scriptwriters, I dare you.
Q1: Cardinals 3, Seahawks 0
Predator : Feels good to mention Nick Emmanwori again.
Prey : Gardner Minshew, who peed his pants a little but the broadcast was too chicken to show it.

How: One of the things that sets really good ball carriers apart is how quickly they get up to full speed. I really like what Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price bring to the table, especially as complements to one another, but Kenneth Walker was so good at accelerating straight from first gear to fifth. Emmanwori does that here and also finds time to maul Minshew with his arms/tentacles.

Minshew was flagged for intentional grounding. When you don’t give a QB time to process, good things happen. Anytime the competition committee wants to change the grounding rule to reward the nearest defender with a sack, they should feel free, by the way.

Recap : Opening the game with three JSN targets is a choice, and I don’t necessarily mind it, and it’s hard to argue it didn’t work, given the later success both Charbs and Price had on the ground. I like Brian Fleury dictating to his Arizona counterpart, or telling him, you think we’re gonna approach this game one ultra-conservative way? Think again.

The plan didn’t result in points, Drew Lock was off target twice and the Seahawks went three-and out. There’s still something to be said for putting the fear of Jax into the opponent’s collective psyche right away.

Pinned on the 1 by Michael Dickson’s sumptuous right foot, the Cardinals drove the length of the field, although as mentioned earlier, if the Reggie Virgil bobble is called correctly, there are no points for them. What was most encouraging of all, was seeing the Seahawks defend the red zone blades of grass like the rest of the blades. They broke an unfortunate string of nine consecutive red zone touchdowns allowed.
And the field goal Chad Ryland knocked through would be his — and his teammates’ — last of the day.
Seattle’s next possession would stall at midfield when Mack Wilson was left unblocked on third down. But no matter, the E-Man would show up as advertised, Arizona punted right back.
Something about Price receiving chops and willingness and he’s explosive so just get him the ball. If you see a little C.J. Prosise in his game after this clip, well, who am I to stop you?

Charbonnet and Price each moved the sticks afterward, the Seahawks knocked on the door, the Cardinals ended the quarter with a brain fart, jumping offsides before the clock ran out, and as the quarter ended, the hosts were poised to take the lead.
Q2: Seahawks 7, Cardinals 6
Predator : Seahawks pass rushers, composite, as the half drew to a close
Prey : Not to pick on him again, but Minshew. Look, he plays the game voluntarily.

How: On the Cardinals’ final five pass plays of the half, Minshew was sacked twice, pressured all five, and completed one pass for two yards, that McBride fumbled. Five different Seahawks got there: Byron Murphy II on third down midway through the quarter, then Lawrence, then Emmanwori, then Ernest Jones won a seven-man race, before Dante Fowler finally finished him off to send everyone to the locker room.
Minshew had been 8/10 with 8.0 YPA until the full weight of the Seattle pass rush fell upon him. He was 13/20 with 3.4 after.

Recap : Two yards from paydirt, the Seahawks stopped getting cute. A.J. Barner took the handoff both times and they helped him scoot his glute for loot. The second thrust was the charm, and Seattle had a lead it would never relinquish.
All 58 yards on the touchdown drive were gained by running backs or rushing plays.
The teams traded punts for the next four possessions, but Murphy’s sack was especially well-timed, as it knocked the Cardinals out of field goal range.

Seems like every week the Seahawks give up an inexplicable points-scoring drive, and with that out of the way, they set out to complete another side quest: scoring in 90 seconds or less. Under two minutes remained. Perfect timing.
A couple completions and some tough Charbonnet running moved the chains. A 29-yard obvious DPI flag got the Seahawks close, and then Jax made his biggest contribution of the day:

With only one timeout you needed an explosive to open up the playbook and go for six instead of three. With a crossing pattern you needed to break tackles. This is why you made the man the highest-paid WR in football.
Barner doesn’t quite hold on, ball moves at he hits the ground and slides along the turf. Didn’t look like a catch but here’s the thing about refereeing decisions: they tend to even out.
Arizona scored three points on a catch that wasn’t and got to punt on an obvious fumble.
Q3: Seahawks 17, Cardinals 3
Predator : I just really appreciated the cool demeanor Drew Lock exuded as he calmly dropped this sidearm throw around a rushing Andrew Wingard.
Prey : Fear and anxiety of getting your sh-t rocked.
How : How indeed.
This catch gave the Seahawks a new set of downs, which they invested in three points later to cap the day’s scoring.

Arizona’s opening possession out of the break ran into the outstretched arm of Josh Jobe on another well-timed corner blitz (how does Macdonald know?!) and a third-down Lawrence sack. Tank is never allowed to retire.

Seattle answered with the game’s final points on a field goal drive saved by Lock’s ability to deal with pressure, as detailed earlier. If he doesn’t have a job here next season he can compete for starter minutes elsewhere, and if so the Seahawks will miss him.

The Cardinals punted for the sixth time in seven possessions, the other being the end of half, ensuring Seattle would hold the ball and a two touchdown lead entering the final quarter. Just as every fan no doubt predicted when the final injury report came out Friday.
Q4: Seahawks 17, Cardinals 3
Predator : Zach Charbonnet
Prey : Rehab

How : Charbs didn’t get to participate in the ritual fourth quarter demoralization of the Cardinals in Week 4, so it’s only he fair he got to convert first downs on consecutive . Also, it’s fair to declare him all the way back from the ACL injury that ended his 2025 season prematurely.
Charbs finished with a 16-77-0 line but 37 of those came in the fourth quarter and he had a monster 25-yard screen pass called back for a personal foul after the play. Which… shouldn’t happen?

The Seahawks offense can now do these types of things to an opposing defense again. Yes, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani did some real men’s work while the team awaited Charbonnet’s return. That being said, he changes the offense, not sure how else to put it. Sometimes the simplest solution verified by the eye test is the most accurate explanation.

Recap : A Kupp conversion opened the fourth quarter, and after Lock got the defense to jump again, for the third time, he found Tory Horton alone in the middle of the field for 17. What’s especially fun about the catch is how JSN made it happen. His mere presence drew two defenders deep. Horton found the belly of the zone, awaited the ball, and got to file it away for next week. Or the looming 49ers game Thanksgiving weekend.

A couple handoffs to Price killed 90 seconds of game clock, and when Lock found Charbonnet as a sideline outlet on third down, and the former Bruin dodged defenders all the way to the 22, it felt like game over for the visitors. Except they would receive one more bailout. Jalen Sundell was flagged for the late hit you can see above; officials somehow decided it erased the play instead of allowing the first down to stand before moving Seattle back 15 yards. Abruptly, the Seahawks were out of field goal range and facing 3rd and 20. They punted, unable to add on or bleed any more clock.

No matter — the Cardinals would run it out on their own. A zero-point drive with an overturned interception and a McBride toe-tapper on fourth down put Arizona on the doorstep, first and goal inside the Seattle five. But Lawrence blew up the first down run, Minshew aborted his scramble at the two yards line, and threw two incompletions to curtail the threat. The Cardinals ran 14 plays for 76 yards in six minutes, only to boost Seattle’s win probability above 99 by the end.
As a parting gift, they also gifted us one last moment for Spoon to the refs what’s what.

Anyway, the Seahawks would ride Charbonnet for the first downs pictured above, run another Barnyard on 3rd and 1 to take us to the two-minute warning, and then engage in a little victory formation, as a treat.
Evening Preyers

Seattle won without a monster game from JSN . A frequent criticism of the offense has been its over-reliance on Smith-Njigba, prompting many to wonder if a path to victory exists when he’s not beating worlds. God to see it, even if the 7-51-0 game slows his history books chase.

No, an opposing running back did not reach 100 yards . In fact, Allgeier and Minshew combined for just 50 on the ground, total. The depth of this defensive line and tackling ability of second-level defenders is unlike anything I’ve seen since 2013.

Brian Fleury had his best game as a play caller . You had the early JSN targets to clear out the box, then 36 runs to 28 passes. Fleury was forced to game plan around backup with one functioning elbow, the non-throwing one. And he earned how to call positive running plays from the 1! Loved to see the Barnyard at the goal line. Our offensive coordinator is
We’ll have to look at time to throw stats too, but he also kept Lock out of danger; no sacks allowed. Which I suppose, if you’re so inclined, you could credit the offensive line too.

And yes, getting your starting ball toters back from injury helps. The Charbonnet-Price RB combo, with decent run blocking of course, is a missing element that’s no longer missing. Those guys would make any coordinator look smarter.

No egregious special teams errors except for illegal formation on a kickoff, which led to exactly zero points. Dickson dropped a punt at the one, Myers made everything, coverage was good and returns were acceptable. A big part of winning double digit games in an NFL season is NOT giving any of them away. As we’ve seen divisional rivals do recently via kicking meltdowns.
Why yes, everyone does get another Witherspoon highlight .

Viewers were fed multiple shots of a stoic Sam Darnold . Watching your team operate with you is probably already hard enough, but witnessing them win in large part because they made no critical errors on offense could be the jolt he needs to buckle down and practice real ball security. Of course, if that was going to work, it would have probably kicked in when he spent most of September on the sideline.

I’m not a Start Drew Lock guy. His limitations are greater than Darnold’s and I want Sam back under center as soon as physically possible. There won’t be any Cardinals-levels opponents in January. And Lock doesn’t win either Rams home game last year. Nevertheless: when a Seahawk quarterback plays within himself and trusts the process, eschews hero ball, and lets his more talented teammates (of which there are many!) decide the game, good things happen to this team. Lock is better at that very specific job, which serves Seattle, Macdonald and Fleury more at this stage of the season.

So I don’t believe there should be any quarterback controversy after the bye, when both men are much healthier. The Seahawks need Drew Lock to play this same game again against the Raiders next Sunday, then
Eight rushing first downs for Seattle after one against Chicago. Would like to officially and permanently reword a mantra I fell for last decade: Running backs don’t matter, until they do.
Finally, another reason pumpkin pie is superior to its siblings is the ease of cutting perfectly shaped pieces without them falling apart on the plate.

Four games in the next five weeks. Well-timed bye, for once? We’ll take it. Niners after. Free-falling Raiders and Cowboys in there somewhere, that’s fortuitous. The J.J. McCarthy Giants too. If the Seahawks are going to make a title defense, officially, like by reaching the playoffs, they’ll need three wins in the next four. Good news: they can do it with the defense they have and the game plan we saw Sunday, while they wait and regain their most impactful players in the trenches.

This season was always fated to be a little weird. But now it has the chance to be special again; if the Seahawks can make the formula work twice in three weeks, once against a contender and again against a rival, they can make it work anytime.

articles.headline: Ramla Ali wins first world titles at 36 with highly controversial split decision
keyFacts: British-Somali boxer Ramla Ali won the vacant WBO and IBF junior featherweight titles at age 36 via a controversial split decision against Mikiah Kreps.
Promoter Lou DiBella and punch statistics questioned the verdict, noting that Kreps landed more punches and outworked Ali during the 10-round bout.
Ali expressed emotional relief after the fight, dedicating her first world title victory to her late father.
body: British-Somali boxer Ramla Ali became a world champion for the first time at the age of 36 on Sunday night after winning a highly controversial 10-round split decision over former sparring partner Mikiah Kreps to claim the vacant WBO and IBF women’s junior featherweight titles in Arlington, Texas.

Ali, who grew up in east London after fleeing Somalia’s civil war with her family and went on to become the first boxer to represent the African country at the Olympics, completed her remarkable journey to the top of the 122lb division at College Park Center on her second attempt at a world championship – but only after a verdict rewarding her for a fight that appeared to be largely controlled by her opponent.

“I can’t put into words what this means to me and what this means to all of Somalia,” a visibly emotional Ali said in the immediate aftermath. “I’ve hopefully inspired so many young girls and boys out there to dream big and that’s all I’ve ever wanted to do.”
Ali (12-2, 3 KOs) took the upper hand early after scoring a knockdown in the third round when Kreps touched the canvas with her glove after taking a right hook flush to the chin.

But Kreps (11-1, 3 KOs) appeared galvanized by the setback, ramping up her volume and applying relentless pressure that disrupted Ali’s rhythm as the 30-year-old American took control of the exchanges and appeared to win the majority of the remaining rounds.
The ringside arbiters were sharply divided, with Ali prevailing by scores of 97-92 and 96-93 while the third judge favored Kreps 98-91. (The Guardian had it 97-92 for Kreps.)

Compubox’s punch statistics only cast further doubt on the decision. Kreps outlanded Ali by 115 blows to 78 overall, including a 91-70 edge in power shots, while connecting on the greater number of punches in eight of the 10 rounds. The New Yorker also threw 525 punches to Ali’s 346, maintaining a substantially higher work rate throughout the contest.

When the scores were announced, an overwhelmed Ali dropped to her knees and wept. She then spoke of her father who died six months ago, saying that her trainer had invoked his memory before the fight.

“When we were in the changing room, my coach said, because my dad passed away in May, ‘Do this for him,’” Ali said during an in-ring interview. “That’s where those emotions came out at the end, because I did it for my dad.”
Ali also paid tribute to Kreps, acknowledging her opponent’s industry and crowding tactics that had made the contest so difficult.
“Every time I went to the corner, I kept saying, ‘I’m so tired. I’m so tired,’ because your work rate was just next level,” she said.
Veteran promoter Lou DiBella, who has increasingly assumed the role of boxing’s unofficial ombudsman, was among those outraged by the verdict, calling for an investigation into the scoring.
“Mikiah Kreps won that fight and it wasn’t close. Stevie Wonder could see that,” DiBella wrote on social media. “Boxing can’t get out of its own way. I am appalled at that decision.”

Ali’s breakthrough came more than two years after her first crack at a world title ended in disappointment, when she lost a 10-round unanimous decision to Yamileth Mercado in a bid for the Mexican’s WBC junior featherweight strap. Her extraordinary life story is the subject of In the Shadows, a biopic starring Top Boy actor Jasmine Jobson that premiered last month.

In the main event, three-belt junior lightweight champion Alycia Baumgardner moved up to 135lb and added the IBF lightweight title with a commanding unanimous decision over Elif Nur Turhan. All three judges scored the fight a 100-90 whitewash for Baumgardner in a contest held under men’s championship rules with 10 rounds of three minutes each.

“What’s next is undisputed, like I did at 130,” Baumgardner said afterward, fixing her sights on a showdown with Britain’s Caroline Dubois, the WBC and WBO lightweight champion who took in Sunday’s fights from ringside.

The pair engaged in a heated ringside confrontation moments later, renewing a feud that has simmered for months. Dubois, 25, has repeatedly accused the American of avoiding her, while Baumgardner has maintained the Briton has yet to earn the right to share a ring with her.

Dubois is scheduled to face Stephanie Han in a 135lb title unification bout on 20 February at the Don Haskins Center in El Paso, Texas, with the WBA, WBC and WBO lightweight belts on the line. Should Dubois prevail, it would set the stage for a four-belt unification fight with Baumgardner for the undisputed 135lb title in what could be one of the biggest fights in women’s boxing in 2027.

Baumgardner’s and Ali’s bouts topped the seventh card staged by Most Valuable Promotions Women, the fledgling women’s boxing series launched by boxer-influencer Jake Paul in March alongside a three-year ESPN broadcast deal designed to give female fighters a regular platform on linear television.

Earlier on the program, Australia’s Skye Nicolson retained her WBC junior featherweight title with a unanimous decision over Japan’s Miyo Yoshida, winning by scores of 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92. Mexico’s Irma Garcia unified the IBF and WBA junior bantamweight titles with a unanimous verdict over Panama’s Nataly Delgado, with all three judges handing down scores of 97-92 after Garcia registered a sixth-round knockdown.

On the preliminary card, Brittany Sims and Shera Mae Patricio fought to a 10-round split draw in their contest for the vacant WBA regular bantamweight championship. One judge favored Sims 97-93, another had Patricio winning 100-90 and the third scored it 95-95, leaving the title unclaimed.

articles.headline: LeBron James reveals why the 76ers have been such a clutch team in the 2026-27 season
keyFacts: LeBron James praised the Philadelphia 76ers for their poise and execution during clutch moments this season.
The 76ers secured a close win against the Chicago Bulls, maintaining an 8-0 record in crunch-time games.
James stated that the team has experienced players with no panic button who know how to remain calm.
body: As one of the most talented teams in the league, it is no surprise that the Philadelphia 76ers are a good team when it comes to execution in the clutch moments. They have some of the league's most dangerous scorers, but at the same time, they also have the sense to make smart decisions.

It is important to note that the 76ers have been hyped as one of the league's best teams ever since they acquired LeBron James and traded for Jaylen Brown. The talent was the most enticing part of the new-look 76ers, but the poise under pressure is something that went under the radar.
LeBron James speaks on the 76ers' ability to thrive in the clutch

When a team has LeBron as the leader, there is always a sense of stability and poise within the team. That is not the only factor helping the 76ers these days because they have the talent to keep up and prove that they are one of the best teams in the league when it comes to the clutch.

Against the Chicago Bulls on Sunday, the 76ers managed to eke out a close win. It was too close for comfort, especially since the Bulls are seen as one of the worst teams in the league. Of course, the 76ers pulled out the victory, and that is because of their poise under pressure.

James himself spoke about the team and had nothing but praise for their ability to stand out in the clutch moments. He is not only praising himself, but the rest of the team that has been having some big moments throughout this season when they have won 8-0 in games that have gone into crunch time.

"We have a lot of guys who have been in late-game situations, and we have a no panic button. We understand that we have to get some stops on this end, but if teams make a run, we understand how to be calm on the other end as well," James said about the 76ers' poise after the victory against the Bulls.

As the 76ers continue to progress this season, it feels like they are going from strength to strength. They are relying on their overwhelming talent to start the year, but they are getting better and better with each game, which should scare the rest of the league.

articles.headline: US President Donald Trump says deportation policy was 'too tough' for voters
keyFacts: US President Donald Trump said his deportation policy was "too tough" for voters and contributed to midterm election losses.
Trump stated he was only joking about offering the White House press secretary job to UFC boss Dana White.
Trump said he will meet Russian and Chinese leaders at next week's APEC summit to discuss ending the Iran war.
body: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said that his deportation policy for undocumented immigrants was "too tough" for voters and he can work with the Democrats in the new Congress to craft an immigration deal.

Speaking during his first major interview since his party lost control of the House and Senate in the midterm election, Trump said his deportation policy may have been part of the reason Republicans lost.
"I think it was too tough," Trump said. "I think it might be too tough, yeah. And a lot of people would say that it’s great. But a lot of people think it’s too tough."
In his interview to CBS that aired on Sunday, Trump said that he can find a way to work with the Democrats.
"The deal would be we would work something out. And I think it's something — I think that's something that's actually doable," he said in the interview.

Trump did not share the details of what the immigration deal would look like but shortly after the interview he appointed Stephen Miller, who designed the Trump administration's hardline deportation policy, as his chief of staff.
In his tenure, Trump's administration has aggressively pushed to deport millions of undocumented migrants which drew widespread criticism.
Trump 'only kidding' about Dana White press secretary job offer
Trump said he was just joking about making Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White his next White House press secretary.
"I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Trump told reporters.
In a social media post Saturday, Trump implored White to accept his offer, writing, "Dana, please take the job!" and calling him a "violent fighter and warrior."
White is a long-time friend of Trump. He has maintained silence on Trump's remarks, saying that he would "have more to talk about" after meeting with Trump on Monday.
The position of the press secretary has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week on the job.
Trump to meet Xi, Putin to end Iran war
Trump on Sunday said that he will be meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at an APEC leaders' summit in China next week to discuss ending the Iran war.

Before flying back to Washington from Florida, Trump while speaking to the media said: "One of the meetings, I think, will be with President Putin and President Xi, and that'll be interesting. We're talking a lot of things, including denuclearization, but we'll be talking a lot of things. We're trying to end the war in Iran."
Russia in October has said that this first of its kind trilateral meeting is "being prepared."
While Trump has mentioned denuclearization as the focus of the meeting, a Wall Street Journal report said that Putin wanted the three-way talks to broker a peace deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

In his interview with CBS Trump said that "I believe we're very close to making a deal" to end the Russia-Ukraine war that would result in a "little bit different shape Ukraine," without sharing any further details.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang: Silicon Valley superstar engulfed by personal scandal
keyFacts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces a board probe after reports that he engaged in an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Huang leads Nvidia, a $4.5 trillion artificial intelligence chip giant central to US competition with China over technology dominance.
Nvidia's board expressed confidence in Huang, and sources told the BBC that his removal is unlikely.
body: - Published
Jensen Huang is one of the technology industry's most high-profile figures.
He rose to prominence as the business he leads - artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia - became one of the world's most valuable companies.
As the face of the AI boom, Huang also became close to Donald Trump as the president pushed for the US to keep its dominance of the technology over China.
The 63-year-old who was once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" and referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan is now mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Who is Jensen Huang?
Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US.
He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.
Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia.
He has an estimated fortune of $155bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine - a biography on Huang, tells the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.
Huang has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Huang.
Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged.
"I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".
Huang has long found himself at the centre of US-China tensions. Trump has repeatedly said the two nations are in a race for dominance.
Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities.

The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.
Since 2022 the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security.

But it means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. In recent years Huang has engaged in a flurry of shuttle diplomacy, dashing between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way.
Sunday's revelations may explain why Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China.
Quarter after quarter of late, Nvidia has been locked out of that lucrative market. Despite his ostensible closeness to Trump, Huang has not managed to wrest this concession from the administration.
What is Nvidia?
Huang founded Nvidia with fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993.
The company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games.
Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates.

"In 2012 these machine learning neural net researchers started to use it for that purpose and Jensen immediately recongnised that this was going to be a massive industry and the future of computing. He began to pour enormous amounts of resources into building what was essentially the AI hardware market," says Witt.

"Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them."
Nvidia is now worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever.

"The first real neural net of modern times on an Nvidia network was Alex Krizhevsky's Alexnet and they trained that on two Nvidia cards in Alex's bedroom. Now we do the same thing but we do it with 200,000 - 300,000 cards and instead of doing it in a bedroom we do it in a giant barn full of computers called a data centre," adds Witt.

"So when you think about a data centre buildout, when you hear the AI infrastructure buildout, Jensen runs a tollbooth. All of that goes through him. And it made his company at least temporarily, the most valuable company in the world."
Nvidia's board has announced a probe following reports by the New York Times that Huang had engaged in a romantic relationship with a woman believed by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
For now, though, Nvidia's board appears to have little appetite for removing Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team".
Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is also no clear successor to the 63-year old tech boss.
Who is Huang's wife?
Huang met his wife Lori at Oregon State University, where she was also studying electrical engineering and was his lab partner.
They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer.
He has credited Lori and Madison for making black leather jackets his signature style.
In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation.
The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn.
Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University.
"Jensen in my conversations with him and in other conversations has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man. That's very important to him," says Witt.

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways. Both of his children work for Nvidia. Spencer and Maddison. The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."
Huang for his part released a statement which said, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
What do we know about the alleged affair?
US officials had concluded that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reports.

She was a top executive at Megaspeed, a data centre company based in Singapore. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked.
Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".
It remains unclear what information Alice Huang â who is also known as Huang Le â allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.
Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment.
When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not.
"We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC.
Additional reporting by Ayeshea Perera in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney

articles.headline: Inside the French drug gangs recruiting children to kill
keyFacts: French drug gangs in Marseille use social media to recruit children across France for drug dealing, torture, and murder.
Official figures show over 10,000 children were involved in French drug trafficking during 2025.
Police say they have arrested about 1,000 DZ Mafia associates since 2024, but online recruitment makes combating gangs increasingly difficult.
body: - Published
Warning: Strong language and descriptions of sexual violence
Although she had just bought hashish from a drug dealer, the woman decided to call the police.
It was because, along with the illegal drugs, she had been handed a note by the young seller during their brief meeting on a Marseille housing estate in 2022.
"We're being held captive and need help. We are 15-years-old," it read.
The teenage dealer, a French court heard earlier this year, was one of two boys being held by a gang which they had both initially approached looking for paid work - albeit illegal.
One boy had been tasked with handling money, the other worked streets around the Frais-Vallon estate. Soon though, bosses had accused them of being responsible for "shortfalls" in takings.
What followed were regular beatings, the court was told, and being forced to dance naked in front of a camera as a form of blackmail. One of the boys was also raped.

Hours after the woman was passed the note, the two teenagers had tried to escape from a second-storey window, injuring themselves in the process. One managed to get away, while the other was caught, beaten and stabbed, but survived.

Arrests were made. Photos on the phone of one of the boys' alleged torturers showed several other young men in a similarly distressed condition. Six men have since been handed hefty sentences for what happened to the two teenagers.
The boys' story highlights the grip that drug gangs hold over parts of France's second city.
While the blend of Mediterranean culture, street art and hip-hop scene has made Marseille a popular tourist destination - beyond the city centre, it is another story.
After months of trying, a BBC team managed to enter this dangerous world - centred on deprived streets and high-rise housing estates in the port city, which police do not enter lightly.
We found an environment where ruthless gangs lure vulnerable young people with promises of easy money, but end up trapping them in a world of drug dealing, brutality and exploitation.

We saw how gangs use social media to recruit hitmen and spoke to several young men caught up in the violence. From prison, one gang member accused of involvement in several murders explained how his "cold-bloodedness" had helped him rise through the ranks.
The city's most powerful gang, DZ Mafia, emerged victorious from a bloody turf war and is now one of the most feared criminal organisations in France.
DZ is the official internet country code for Algeria, where one of the gang's founders, a French-Algerian called Mehdi Laribi, was detained earlier this year under a French arrest warrant.

The criminal outfit rose to prominence in 2023, when it became the first French gang to capitalise on its notoriety by releasing video statements - using social media to market itself as a brand - says the head of the country's anti-drug trafficking unit, Dimitri Zoulas.
Its most recent statement came in July, when the mayor of a nearby town had to be placed in police protection, after intelligence suggested he was in danger of being targeted by the group.
In an online video, six masked men dressed in black stood behind a table - as one of them read a statement denying DZ Mafia's involvement.
France's expanding illegal drugs market - which has seen a surge in cocaine imports alongside high volumes of cannabis and synthetic drugs - has also helped the gang grow rapidly.

The number of cocaine users in France is expected soon to reach two million, says Zoulas, up from 600,000 in 2017. Drug smuggling across France generates â¬7bn (Â£5.9bn) a year, involving 200,000 people, he adds.

Many of those distributing the drugs are children and the authorities say the number of minors caught up in trafficking is increasing. During 2025, more than 10,000 children were involved in some way, according to official figures.
DZ Mafia is a prime example. To reach more customers, it needs more gang members - more children.
We have found it is now recruiting young people from across France - not just to sell drugs, but to carry out kidnap, torture and murder.
They are a generation seen as easy to corrupt, but also expendable, by the kingpins who typically control them from prison or overseas.
And, as police and judges warn, once these children enter Marseille's underworld, it is very hard to get them out.
Few know the human cost of Marseille's gangs like mother Karine Brouillard - who lives at the other end of France, almost as far from the Mediterranean coast as you can get.

Her son, Hugo, first ran away aged 15 - from his home in a village in the Nord department - after an argument with his family. He was picked up by police three days later, almost 1,000km (600 miles) away in Marseille, with money and cannabis on him. He was taken home.
But several years later, in 2023, Hugo planned to return south, telling his parents he had secured a holiday job at a restaurant near Marseille.
"He gave regular updates," Karine remembers. "He called me, everything was going well."
Three weeks later, a doctor called. Karine says she will never forget his words: "Your son arrived last night. He took a bullet to the head."
Police believe Hugo was brought for medical help from a gang-controlled area and suspect he was involved with one.
That area was Quartier Nord.
Our best way into Quartier Nord, where DZ Mafia wields power, is with the help of resident Fadella Ouidef, a 41-year-old mother-of-four who gives us a tour.
Thirty-seven seconds after entering one housing estate, we find ourselves cornered.

Car horns sound the moment Fadella's Peugeot passes a gang checkpoint - the teenagers manning the post immediately spot our camera. "Wait, stop filming," Fadella warns, as a grey 4x4 forces us to the side of the road.
"I'm making a report for my housing association," she tells the inquisitive driver. He eventually agrees to let us leave if we stop filming.
It is unnerving to see a non-police vehicle move so assertively and a relief to watch it leave.
"Lately, the gangs have been very aggressive," explains Fadella. "What we simply try to do is make sure our young people understand what's happening is wrong."
Fadella speaks to a wider fear among local families: that their children are enticed by huge sums of money to take a criminal path that robs them of their innocence.
Money is what led one young man to spend his teenage years with DZ Mafia.
In order for our interviewees to speak freely, or because of safety concerns, we have agreed to protect their identities.
Camil tells us he worked up the gang's ranks to "running security" in one area it controls.
The now 20-year-old, who claims to have left the group, is highly suspicious of our presence, but agrees to tell us how the gang recruits young members.
"They know how to get inside your head. Whatever you want, they give to you," he says. This can range from nice cars and spacious apartments, to drugs and prostitutes, he explains.
"You feel loyalty because of what they give you. You'll stay until the very end, until either death or prison."
Camil also gives a sobering assessment of what happens if the gang identifies a weakness in a recruit: "They'll exploit it. You're their bitch, it's over."
DZ Mafia member, Adam - not his real name - tells us he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad when we speak to him in a Snapchat video call.
He is currently in prison awaiting trial, after being implicated in several murders.
"People noticed my determination, my cold-bloodedness and, without wanting to, I climbed up the ladder of the gang," says Adam. "It became my place, I had to roll with it."
During the chat, he agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking".

"Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jamsâ¦ it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well."
We challenge Adam on whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality.
He says he is "feeling in-part guilty" but claims to have no regrets.
"If I hadn't done all of this, there are other people who would have done that in my place, and so on. I am just another brick in the wall," he says.
Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap".
At a so-called deal point in a social housing estate - sealed off and controlled by DZ Mafia - price lists for cocaine, hashish and marijuana are graffitied on a wall.
The estate acts as a natural fortress for drug dealers. With one major road in and out, they can control the flow of customers and see if the police are coming.
It is not uncommon for the sound of automatic gunfire to fill the night air in these areas.
After months of negotiations, a deal-point manager from a rival gang agrees to meet us where he works.
We enter the estate early in the morning, the birdsong and children walking to school providing a stark contrast to the industrial-scale criminal operation that takes place here.
"Joe" says he was making â¬3,000 (Â£2,500) a month when he was 13. Now he says that has risen to between â¬5,000 and â¬10,000 a month.
He seems to see his life path as pre-ordained, albeit a lucrative one.
We ask Joe if he thinks about the lives lost because of the violence carried out by his gang, but the 23-year-old has also long made peace with the pain and destruction drug trafficking can cause.
"It destroys people, but we all make our own choices," he shrugs.
The work that Joe's gang and DZ Mafia are doing represents a threat to national security, says Zoulas, of the anti-drug trafficking unit.
There are road accidents, as well as family violence, depressions, suicides and more than 700 overdoses each year, he says, "and it distorts the economy".
"We are heading towards a potential systemic breakdown of the criminal justice system."
Police have had success in Marseille and other cities against drug gangs.
Criminal operations are being frustrated, more kingpins arrested and drugs seized.
Since 2024, about 1,000 individuals associated with DZ Mafia have been arrested, and 600 incarcerated, police say.
But overall, it is a battle that is becoming more arduous, rather than easier.

As gangs seek to widen their operations, or replace members who have been arrested or killed, social media has become a potent recruitment tool - especially since the Covid pandemic, when many street-drug sales jumped online.
On social media, we found countless posts advertising jobs in Marseille for aspiring drivers, couriers and hitmen, often with glamourised AI-generated images.
Nets are also being cast wider, as it becomes harder to entice young people locally because they know more about what might happen to them.
The ads can reach teenagers in most corners of France - including Paris, Nantes and Lille - and serve as a powerful pull to Marseille, and the Quartier Nord, police say.
Online advertising has also changed the typical profile of someone who would join a gang's ranks, say law enforcement officials.
Now, it is often someone without a criminal past, but who has exploitable vulnerabilities, like having a difficult family life.
"These people are recruited by unscrupulous sponsors who send them into the lion's den," explains Thibaut Fontaine, the head of France's anti-organised-crime unit.
Their lack of criminal experience, he says, makes them easier to arrest quickly.
Karine still has no idea why her son, Hugo, was shot.

Asked what she would say to gang leaders recruiting children and young men in Marseille, she says: "They destroy families. Little sisters, little brothers, grandparents. But then, I don't think those people have a heart, really."
The restaurant where her son said he was going to work did exist, but staï¬ there told Karine they had never recruited anyone called Hugo.
The reason for his death almost certainly lies within Marseille's Quartier Nord.
Additional reporting by Marianne Baisnee, Lea Guedj and Paul Pradier

articles.headline: Democrats to attend Cop31 climate talks boosted by midterms and eager to make up for Trump-era setbacks
keyFacts: About 20 Democratic lawmakers are attending the Cop31 climate summit using philanthropic funding after the Trump administration refused to participate.
Delegates said the Democrats' midterm victory winning control of Congress boosted international optimism for future United States climate action.
Democrats plan to use subpoena powers and budget control in January to scrutinize administration actions and restore environmental funding.
body: The US will be absent from key UN climate talks that start on Monday, a further sign of Donald Trump’s scornful dismissal of the climate crisis. But Democrats’ crushing win in the US midterm elections has delivered a timely shot of optimism to countries now looking beyond the Trump era of climate obstruction.

For the second year in a row, there will be no official US government presence at the annual climate summit, this year known as Cop31 and held in Antalya, Turkey. While almost every other country in the world sends delegations to the talks, Trump has derided the climate crisis as a “hoax” and “bullshit” and triggered the withdrawal of the US from the entire international climate framework.

“This summit rejects reality by failing to acknowledge that extremist climate policies are destroying countries around the world,” a White House official said, confirming that the administration would not send anyone to Cop31.

The snub is so severe that about 20 members of the US Congress heading to the summit have been denied usual state department assistance, requiring them to turn to philanthropic funding for the trip. “I’m glad we found a way to get there, but it is insane,” said Sean Casten, a Democratic congressman who is attending Cop31. “We have a lot of rebuilding to do. It hinges on Congress to maintain diplomatic continuities at Cop and minimize the damage until adults are back in the White House.”

Trump’s active support of fossil fuels, evisceration of pollution limits and throttling of clean energy projects has caused the US to become an outlier among wealthy countries, a recent UN report found. While all the other 20 major economies reduced or slowed their carbon pollution last year, the US was a “major exception” by emitting an extra 133m tons of planet-heating gases from the burning of coal, oil and gas, the report states.

Despite the world rapidly surging past “safe” temperature thresholds because of such pollution, and escalating heatwaves, floods, droughts and other calamities, Trump has remained defiant. “If you don’t get away from this green scam, your country is going to fail,” the US president told other world leaders at the UN last year, adding that the climate crisis was “the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world”.

But the Democrats’ stunning success in the midterms last week, wresting control from Trump’s Republicans in both the House of Representatives and the Senate, has buoyed delegates gathering in Antalya. While this will be the last Cop with the US as an official party, after Trump exited the UN framework, the midterms have raised international confidence of a looming return and new, post-Trump chapter.

“This marks the beginning of the end of the Trump era,” said Mohamed Adow, director of Power Shift Africa. “His grip on Congress has been broken and hopefully paves the way for a Democratic president in two years. For everyone fighting for a livable planet, this is a moment of renewed hope.”

Trump has done “enormous damage” to the climate but the midterms results, along with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s recent electoral victory in Brazil, provides a major tonic, Adow said. “It opens the door to America returning to the climate fight with the seriousness its responsibility demands,” he said, adding that Cop31 would be the “perfect time to accelerate climate action and turn the tide on the Trump dark ages”.

US lawmakers arriving at Cop, all of them Democrats, are aware the world has long been subjected to wildly erratic US commitment to climate action, Casten acknowledged. “We go in with a fair amount of humility – as important as we are, the US has been an extremely unreliable partner on climate,” he said. “But going to Cop on the heels of these results feels a lot better. It can be a much more positive process now.”

Spanning two weeks of negotiations among 197 countries with an accompanying trade show-like jamboree of pavilions and side events interspersed by protests, the sprawling Cop process requires a sense of momentum. The electoral revolt in the US, the world’s largest historical emitter of greenhouse gases, should provide such a fillip, according to Susan Biniaz, a former longtime climate negotiator for the US at Cop.

“Much of the world is looking to the midterms for some kind of signal from the US electorate that they are unhappy with this administration,” Biniaz said. “This could elevate the mood. I don’t think the midterm elections will directly affect federal climate policy but they will help the spirit of the Cop.”

“There’s been a big shift since the midterms. I’m certainly more optimistic,” said Catherine McKenna, former environment minister of Canada. “Negotiations at Cop are important but it’s more important what happens at home and Trump has been incredibly disruptive. We will now have more Democrats acting on climate and talking about the solutions that will actually save people money.”

But what will a thumping Democratic majority in Congress be able to do on climate? Sweeping climate legislation, similar in scale to the Inflation Reduction Act signed by Joe Biden that was subsequently gutted by Republicans, is not likely given Trump’s veto power. Still, Democrats are exploring other avenues.

Investigative and subpoena powers will be used to probe parts of the administration, such as the Environmental Protection Agency, over staff cuts and what Democrats call the “unlawful” withholding of climate and clean energy spending. Trump’s attempt to pressure Europe into taking US gas will be scrutinized, as will the vulnerability of the insurance industry to the climate crisis and concerns over the US ceding clean tech industries to China.
Democrats will dominate the budget process and will likely reverse funding cuts to environmental programs and rein in datacenters, which have become highly contentious with the US public.

Some legislation, such as the speeding up of the permitting process to allow new clean energy production and transmission, may be possible with Republican support too. The midterms also delivered striking Democratic wins at the state level, bringing new governors to states such as Texas and Georgia, meaning widespread state-based action to shift away from fossil fuels will be possible.

Much of this will likely be framed as helping tackle the rising cost of living or government corruption, rather than the climate crisis itself. Some activists have criticized Democrats for so-called “climate hushing” even as most people in the US favor the end of the fossil fuel era, but Casten said emissions reductions will matter more to the new Congress than rhetoric.

“We are going to do everything – oversight, legislation and action through the courts,” he said. “There are things around the cost of gas, or housing and insurance that are climate conversations even if we don’t mention climate. It’s our job to understand how all those things are connected but we have to talk about climate change to people in a way that is salient to them. It’s not that we don’t want to talk about climate change at all.”

Regardless of how Democrats talk about the climate crisis, its effects are mounting. Scientists have warned, repeatedly, that sluggish progress in cutting emissions has left little time to avoid disastrous impacts.

The world is already set to overshoot the internationally agreed target of limiting the global temperature rise to 1.5C, locking in turmoil for people, wildlife and ecosystems around the world, and any lingering embrace of fossil fuels by major emitters like the US will only worsen this pain. When Democrats take over Congress in January, advocates will clamor for them to rapidly make up for lost time.

“They have to do more than hold the line – this was a sweeping mandate for change,” said Rachel Cleetus, program director with the climate program at the Union of Concerned Scientists. “The science is sobering. It’s not going to wait for the next election cycle. This is a reality that people are dealing with right now and responsible lawmakers have to recognize that. The world is eager for the US to step up.”

articles.headline: Madrid matadors and indestructible Mahomes - NFL Sunday Review
keyFacts: Cincinnati Bengals stars Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins defeated the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid.
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes overcame a first-half arm injury scare to secure a victory.
The New York Giants are pursuing a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the Tuesday deadline.
body: Patrick Mahomes proves he is indestructible while Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins light up Madrid - NFL Sunday Review

NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on Week Nine in the NFL as the Cincinnati Bengals stars dazzled in Madrid, Patrick Mahomes overcame an injury scare and Myles Garrett made an emphatic return from injury in his first big day for the Los Angeles Rams
Monday 9 November 2026 06:17, UK

Want to grow the NFL overseas? Send the stars. The superstars. The Joe Burrows'. The Ja'Marr Chases'. The Tee Higgins'. Let them flourish like superstars, and watch new host countries turn to disciples.

Thousands of Spanish fans will have left the Bernabeu on Sunday with either a strengthened or a new-found connection to the Bengals, who delivered about as good a product as you are likely to see in an international game as they beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 on the league's return to Madrid.

A winning product. A Super Bowl-contending product. The product of a three-headed monster capable of taking a sledgehammer to any defense in football, and one built to thrive amid the fiercest of slugfests.
Find yourself in a shoot-out with these Bengals and you are likely to come out second best. Particularly against this version of Burrow.

- Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
There is a growing argument this version is flirting with the best version of Burrow in his NFL career as he seeks to fulfil his own rallying cry for Championship urgency this past offseason.

He was insistent "this is it" as far as Cincinnati's Super Bowl quest was concerned, long-tired of slow starts and injury setbacks that have hindered their mission to get back to the 'Big Dance', where they fell short against the Los Angeles Rams four years ago.

Burrow was near-flawless on European soil as he threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for another himself, which he capped by imitating a Neymar celebration. Whether the Brazilian icon played for Real or not, the locals enjoyed it, so too his admiration for the city's museum scene this week.
"I always whisper in his ear to be legendary. That's who he is and that's what he does," Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence told Sky Sports NFL.
"He's the greatest. We keep calling him a killer - he goes out there with that look in his eye and does what he's supposed to do and puts point on the board."

Head coach Zac Taylor admitted after the game the difficulty in resisting temptation to make every play a passing play such has been Burrow's dominance this season. As much was evident in his reply to Atlanta's opening touchdown when he launched deep to Chase for the 47-yard touchdown that would open the floodgates for Cincinnati's command.
"When I saw that first touchdown I was like 'uh oh', it was a snowball effect," said Higgins after the game.

It represented their 19th touchdown connection of at least 40 yards to tie Joe Montana and Jerry Rice for the third-most by a quarterback-receiver duo since 1980, behind only Peyton Manning and Marvin Harrison (21) and Steve Young and Rice (20).

It is unfair. It is rude. It should be illegal to have a Chase-Higgins pairing at the disposal of a full-flow Burrow; together they are borderline unstoppable. There was a moment during Higgins' second touchdown of the game when both myself and a colleague pointed towards Chase, who had also wriggled free in the end zone to give Burrow a dream pick-your-poison scenario.
There are defensive coordinators across the NFL that might relate to Higgins' 'uh oh' sentiment upon a Burrow-Chase union. It tends to spell trouble, and there tends to be zero remedies.

The celebration of choice on Chase's touchdown was a matador display as Higgins played the role of charging bull, much to the delight of the Bernabeu crowd. The game's chief protagonists were winning both on the football field but also in the realm of international fandom.
"The fans liked it, 'we did it and I heard them say 'Oleeee'," Higgins said.

There are plenty more 'Oles' to follow this season for an offensive trio playing at a different level to most in the league right now. Discussion surrounding the Bengals' Super Bowl aspirations has usually come back to question marks over their defense, which is why their offseason trade for Dexter Lawrence felt like a potential needle-moving moment.

The reality, though, is that defensive improvement never really needed to be needle-moving or transformative, but instead a meaningful step forward. That is courtesy of a luxury to which few can attest in a trio of Burrow, Chase and Higgins.

Higgins is automatic with one of the safest pairs of suction hands in football and the catch radius to defy any angle or the tightest of man coverage. Chase is a demon with the ball in his hands and a single high safeties worst nightmare come true. So long as that three-headed monster remains intact, the Bengals can challenge for the Super Bowl.
What we learned
- Patrick Mahomes is seemingly indestructible. Robert Saleh - the now Tennessee Titans head coach - once said of the Kansas City Chiefs QB: "Don't be fooled by his little old man jog".

- The three-time Super Bowl winner played through a high ankle sprain in leading KC back from a double-digit deficit to beat the Philadelphia Eagles to one of those titles, while he also overcame turf toe to reach another Super Bowl (which they would lose to Tom Brady's Tampa Bay Buccaneers).

- When it looks like this man might be done, he is not. And that was very much the case again on Sunday when Mahomes' throwing arm appeared to be badly injured on a strip-sack by the New York Jets' David Bailey just before half-time - the Chiefs only leading 14-12 at the time.

- There were some hugely concerned faces on the sideline, none more so than the man himself, as well as tight end buddy Travis Kelce. But, incredibly, after a bit of treatment, No 15 was ready to go again, leading his team on a second-half tear to secure a comfortable 23-point victory in the end.
- The New York Giants are seemingly eyeing a trade for Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, with Big Blue head coach John Harbaugh saying "those conversations are taking place".
- Fox Sports reported on Sunday morning that the Giants had already offered the Colts second and fifth-round draft picks for Taylor, which has not yet got the deal done.

- But the Giants, currently in the driver's seat in the NFC East, are keen to get a deal done with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) missing Sunday's win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Tyrone Tracy Jr (hamstring) on injured reserve and Devin Singletary returning only 31 yards on 21 carries in Philly.

- Taylor, meanwhile, acknowledged he might have played his last game in Indy. "This place helped shape me into the man I am today, so I'm very grateful," Taylor said after their home loss to the Dallas Cowboys. "If it is [my last game], I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis."
- The trade deadline is on Tuesday November 10.
Overreaction or reality?

The Bengals do not need to trade for Jonathan Taylor. 'Need' is a strong word, and there are two sides to the equation when it comes to a potential move for a star running back. Cincinnati want the ball in the hands of their quarterback as much as humanly possible - would it be right and would it be wise to add a centre-piece running back to a scheme that is not only built but functions on shot-gun aerial bombardment?

The other side is the Thanos 'final Infinity Stone' notion to pairing Taylor with Burrow, Chase and Higgins, which becomes every bit the Avengers of NFL offenses and the kind capable of steamrolling its way to a Super Bowl appearance. Taylor is a field-flipper and an immediate difference-maker - but how different do you really want this offense to look?

Chase Brown barely gets a sniff in comparison to other backs around the league; when the Bengals did call on his number in Madrid he helped pave the way for Higgins' second touchdown catch. Sure, it would be box office. But to say the Bengals need him would be a disservice to just how good their prized trio are.
Winners and losers
Winners:

Myles Garrett: A warm welcome back to the Rams for Mr Myles Garrett. Los Angeles' 20-13 road win over the Washington Commanders has them over .500 for the first time in a season which they were expected to dominate - in large part due to their blockbuster offseason addition of the two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, who has been missing due to injury since their season opener.

But he is back, and with a vengeance, as he returned three sacks against the Commanders, the first of which being a forced fumble. Finally paired with three-time DPOY Aaron Donald on the defensive line, the Rams having won three straight, maybe a Super Bowl run could still be on the cards?

Christian Watson and Matthew Golden: The Green Bay Packers are explosive on offense! And the great beneficiaries of Jordan Love continuing to air it out - and coach Matt LaFleur laying the table for him to do so - are receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

Watson came down with 171 yards and a score off seven catches, while Golden 164 off 10 grabs and too found the end zone - career highs for both - as Green Bay put up 45 points on a Pats defense that practically carried them through the playoffs and to the Super Bowl last season. Don't sleep on the Packers.
Losers:
The Chargers gonna keep Chargering. If you thought it could not get any worse for head coach Jim Harbaugh, OC Mike McDaniel, QB Justin Herbert and the still-winless Chargers, you would be wrong!

This Los Angeles offense stinks! Do not let a couple of fourth-quarter, garbage-time touchdowns fool you. The Chargers were trailing 38-9 prior, notching three field goals to go with four punts, an interception, turnover on downs and fumble from their other offensive series.
They are now 0-8 on a truly dismal season.

Dan Quinn: In a Washington Commanders season defined by late offensive blunders or clock mismanagement, their head coach might well have dropped the ball once more to potentially signal curtains for him in the country's capital.

Down seven, on the final play of their loss to the Los Angeles Rams - set up just beyond their opponents' 30-yard line - the Commanders opted to go for a short pass followed by a couple of lame attempts at laterals, rather than take a shot at the end zone.
After the game, Quinn admitted he was "not happy with the execution of that play".

Well, file it alongside Jayden Daniels' sack in the dying seconds of overtime as their Week Five game against the New York Giants ended in a tie, as well as Quinn seeming to forget what down it was a week later in the loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
Player of the Weekend - Arvell Reese, LB, New York Giants

The Philadelphia Eagles are there to be preyed on at the moment, and the New York Giants willingly obliged. Linebacker Arvell Reese in particular feasted to bolster his Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign, logging three sacks, 12 tackles, three tackles for loss, a forced fumble, four pressures and three quarterback hits to torment Eagles back-up quarterback Joe Milton in a 19-11 victory. His 2.29 seconds to sack marked the fastest time in the NFL this season, according to Next Gen Stats. The Giants have a superstar stalwart on their hands.
Game of the Weekend
Sean Payton's Denver Broncos only know how to win close games. In fact, Sunday's 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers means they have now won 16 straight one-score games.
The Broncos survived late when Nik Bonitto strip-sacked Bryce Young and recovered the loose fumble with 1.24 remaining, before Bo Nix clinched the win with a quarterback sneak on third down.

It was what has become typical late Broncos drama. Denver had trailed by one point entering the fourth quarter, meaning it would become their fifth victory of the year after trailing in the fourth. For a large part of the game Young had been sizzling, only to be hit by Broncos defiance.
